paper_title: Knowledge Crosswords Geometric Knowledge Reasoning with Large Language   Models
caption: Problem distribution based on the correctness under the w/ knowledge and w/o knowledge settings using Zero-Shot.
model_annotation: The image displays three pie charts labeled "easy," "medium," and "hard," representing the distribution of problem correctness under different knowledge conditions in a zero-shot setting. Each chart is divided into four segments corresponding to combinations of knowledge availability: N+K+ (teal), N−K+ (beige), N−K− (orange), and N+K− (red), as indicated by the legend on the right. In the "easy" chart, the largest segment is N+K+ at 55.4%, followed by N−K+ at 38.3%, N−K− at 4.6%, and N+K− at 1.7%. In the "medium" chart, N+K+ is again the largest at 58.8%, followed by N−K+ at 35.4%, N−K− at 4.8%, and N+K− at 1.0%. In the "hard" chart, the largest segment is N−K+ at 37.3%, followed by N−K− at 37.9%, N+K+ at 18.1%, and N+K− at 6.7%. The charts visually emphasize the dominance of the N+K+ condition in easier problems, while in harder problems, the N−K− condition becomes nearly equal to N−K+ in size, and N+K+ drops significantly. All percentages are labeled within their respective slices, and the charts are arranged horizontally with the label "Zero-Shot" centered beneath them.
